newsitem.title: JORDAN: Palestinians want settlement halt to revive peace.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians want settlement halt to revive peace.

text.p: Palestinian peace negotiator Nabil Shaath said on Sunday a halt to a Jewish settlement drive in the West Bank was necessary to revive Israeli-Palestinian talks.

Shaath said Israeli willingness to implement overdue steps under 1993 peace accords with the Palestinians could also pave the way for the resumption of talks, frozen since Israel broke ground on a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

"We cannot go towards the final status talks before the end of settlement building, but we can complete the measures relating to the transitional phase which the Israelis have delayed implementing so far," Shaath told reporters in Amman after talks with Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali.

Shaath cited Israel's obstruction of the Palestinian airport and harbour in Gaza, foot-dragging over a safe passage corridor between Gaza and the West Bank, along with a delay in releasing prisoners and redeploying troops from the West bank.
"Their delay in implementing it constitutes complete loss of trust and credibility in the peace process," Shaath said.

But Shaath said resolving these issues was not an alternative to halting Jewish settlement in the occupied territories, which was a prerequisite to moving on to talks on the final status of Palestinian self-rule.
"If we succeed in the coming few days and in my view the hope is slim, but if we succeed then the issue of halting settlements...will be the issue," Shaath added.

Shaath later met King Hussein and handed him a letter from Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on "the latest developments in the Palestinian-Israeli track and the crisis facing the peace process", the state news agency Petra said.
King Hussein was quoted by Petra as stressing the need to exert "all efforts to overcome the obstacles facing the peace process."

Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah told reporters the kingdom supported the Palestinians on the necessary steps needed to revive peace talks, saying there was a "very clear wish by the Palestinians to have peace prevail".

"Everyone feels the negotiating deadlock which the Palestinian-Israel track has reached. There is international support which we feel in all places all over the world for the Palestinians," Tarawnah added.
"There are clear issues for implementation, which should be immediately implemented (by Israel) and there is the final status talks, which should have been started a long while ago," he added.
"There is fairness in the Palestinian demands and the Jordanian position needless to say is fully supportive of the Palestinian position and Egyptian efforts undertaken now,"
In comments broadcast this week, King Hussein has blamed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for a breakdown in the peacemaking.
